exposure: Time points during the first 48 hours of life (6h, 12h, 24h, 48h)
outcome: Basal ganglia perfusion (measured by fractional moving blood volume - FMBV)
cohort: The study included 24 preterm infants examined with serial cranial ultrasounds.
finding: Basal ganglia blood flow, measured by FMBV, significantly increased in preterm infants during the first 48 hours of life as their cerebral circulation adapted to extrauterine life.
